title: Sorted Output from a Binary Search Tree
statement: A binary search tree (BST) keeps smaller values in the left subtree and values that are equal or larger in the right subtree. Read n integers. Insert them one by one into an empty BST, in the given order. Then walk the tree in-order (left, node, right) and print every value. Equal values are all kept. Send equal values to the right.
inputFormat: The first line has n. The second line has n integers separated by spaces.
outputFormat: One line with all n integers in non-decreasing order, separated by single spaces.
constraints: Duplicates may appear and must all be printed
explanations: Inserting 5, 3, 8, 1, 4, 7, 9 builds a tree. An in-order walk visits values from smallest to largest.
The values 10 and -2 appear twice. Both copies are kept, so the output has six numbers in sorted order.
reference:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
vals = [int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n]]
print(" ".join(str(v) for v in sorted(vals)))
